One of my favorite arrangements of all time would be 彼岸帰航 ～ View of The River Styx by Demetori from their album 曼衍珠汝華 ～ Nada Upasana Pundarika. This is probably my favorite Touhou arrangement from my favorite group. Despite being a metal song, 彼岸帰航 ～ View of The River Styx actually invokes a wistful feeling for a lot of the song. It starts out with a rather calm acoustic guitar line before the more upbeat metal guitar kicks in. The whole song is in a minor key, so it has a bit a sad, uneasy feeling to it. The highlight of the track is how masterfully it switches from the energetic electric guitar to the much more calm acoustic portions. I honestly think it fits Komachi perfectly. It captures her lazy, easygoing side for the more quiet parts but she does have a job to do that does get done occasionally, which is in the heavy parts. Also, since she is the guide for those crossing into the afterlife and the wistfulness of the song comes out from that. Finally, Komachi's job is pretty fucking metal in concept, so it fits there too. It is absolutely worth a listen if you even mildly enjoy instrumental metal.

I'll do a second track from the album since I'm on a roll. 霊知の太陽信仰　～ Nuclear Fusion. This is the exact opposite from 彼岸帰航 ～ View of The River Styx. The entire song is pure energy with no breaks in intensity. This song is actually a bit exhausting to listen to and, thankfully, is one of the shortest tracks on the album, any longer and the song would become grating. It actually gives the feeling of fighting for your life in a "duel with the devil" kind of way. It's upbeat but ominous, fast and intense. I would say it's fits how I feel fighting Utsuho rather than fitting her character. Touhou 11 is the only game I have not beaten, mostly because of stage 5 and Utsuho's last spellcard.

Apparently today was Eirin day... who knew. I can never keep track of character days. In celebration of my favorite character's arbitrary day, I decided to do something different this week: I'm going to give my thoughts on an entire album: 悠夜永翔 ～Endless Flight of Eternal Night. I really could not just mention one song on this album, it is meant to be listened to in one sitting as a gapless album (Yukari would be disappointed). Just grab your drink of choice and sit down for roughly an hour of the best Touhou rock cover albums I've ever heard.

悠夜永翔 ～Endless Flight of Eternal Night covers the majority of the tracks in Imperishable Night in the order that one would hear them while playing. Naturally, the first track is the intro 永夜抄 ～ Eastern Night. I don't have much to say about this one. It functions as a gradual build up to the next track with some night insect cries which can be heard at the beginning and the end of the song.

The cries build into the next track, 幻視の夜 ～ Ghostly Eyes, and abruptly met with an electric guitar riff. 幻視の夜 ～ Ghostly Eyes covers the stage 1 theme of the same name. The original track is a bit laid-back and relaxed, but with a hint of anticipation and mystery. This cover has none of that. It full of intensity and energy and leaves me feeling more anticipation than anything else. It seems like the beginning of a journey. My favorite part of the song is probably the guitar solo starting at 5:28, it just sounds really awesome to me for some reason.

After a brief pause, 蠢々秋月 ～ Mooned Insect starts to play. Like the previous song, it is much faster and upbeat than the original. Not much to say about this one either. It plays it safe and does not deviate from the original much. It’s pretty much just a hard rock cover of蠢々秋月 ～ Mooned Insect.

Next is もう歌しか聞こえない. This is my least favorite track for the album. It over stays it’s welcome a bit for me, and is quite repetitive. Like the previous track it is a hard rock cover of the original with few changes made. Not to interesting in my opinion.

As soon as 懐かしき東方の血 started playing, I knew UI-70 were starting to get serious with this album. The first 40 seconds are a slow, deliberate, intense build up to the chorus of the song. Unlike previous covers, this one differentiates itself from the original by changing the cadence a little bit. It is still a hard rock song, but it has a bit of a jazzy swing feel to the melody. Everything in this song works. It’s upbeat, intense, and keeps the interludes interesting enough to keep interesting. I have to point out the guitar riffs on the original melody from 3:01 to 3:24. Everything seems to work for this segment. It sounds awesome and is one of the most memorable parts of the album.

After a short pause 恋色マスタースパーク starts, and oh man, is this song intense. It catches the upbeat and intense nature of the original, and turns it up to 11. For those who have played the game, this fits the chase through the second part of the level perfectly. In short: the song is fast, intense, and energetic. I would say that it is actually a bit too intense. Like 霊知の太陽信仰　～ Nuclear Fusion by Demetori, it can be a bit overwhelming and tiring to listen to.

After the intensity of恋色マスタースパーク, the start of シンデレラケージ ～ Kagome-Kagome comes as a short breather with its acoustic opening. Even though this song is very close to the original, I really like this song. The melody is catchy and easy to hum along with. I have a hard time stopping myself from attempting to hum along with it. Overall, the song is a lot calmer and mysterious sounding than the previous two pieces. It is still has the energy of a UI-70 hard rock song, but the minor key and slower tempo lead to a much different feel than before. It ends on an acoustic portion, which slows down the tempo and slowly subtracts instruments. It brings everything full circle to the beginning of the song and creates anticipation for the next track.

狂気の瞳 ～ Invisible Full Moon is the next track. Like 恋色マスタースパーク it is much more intense than the original, though not as extreme. It is a pretty standard hard-rock cover of the original. It is one of the weaker pieces on the album, but it does not overstay its welcome. A somewhat enjoyable piece, but nothing special.

ヴォヤージュ1969 serves as a short interlude and break from the intensity. It is an all acoustic cover and is actually much faster paced than you would think. It keeps the intensity and anticipation going while still being a bit of a breather from the intensity of the previous couple of tracks. It is a good cover, but it only works in this album. It just does not have the same effect on its own.

千年幻想郷 ～ History of the Moon starts out with a very quiet, and low key guitar solo for the first minute. I really like the opening. It is very calm and deliberate, sort of like the calm before a big boss battle. The opening is even slower and quitter than ヴォヤージュ1969 and brings up the anticipation even more. Then the 1:00 mark hits, and the metal guitar starts. It builds and builds and builds, until the 1:30 mark where the main melody kicks in. Like many other covers in this album it is fast, intense, and energetic. The rest of the song is pretty standard, but the buildup is incredible. Just when the song starts to be a bit tiring, it cools down a bit a short acoustic portion comes from 3:37 to 3:52 as a short breather before the second half of the track. A second breather comes in the form of a piano section preforming the scales from the original from 4:45 to 4:59, which is then joined with the guitar for just about the rest of the song. The song ends on a very intense note compared to previous songs. There is no slow down, it just ends abruptly creating silence.

At this point, there is still 15 minutes left in the album, and there are only two tracks left. That’s because竹取飛翔 ～ Lunatic Princess is a 13 minute long epic of a piece. It opens slowly like千年幻想郷 ～ History of the Moon, but does not take long to build up and quickly becomes a pretty standard cover until the 3:18 mark. The song slows down, slowly adding in a guitar riff or two until 4:12 where it slows down even further and repeats the melody until 4:42. The tempo picks back up for the main melody for a while until 5:47, where a piano arrangement of ヴォヤージュ1970 suddenly takes over. The entire tone of the song changes to a very mysterious and much less intense portion of the song. At one point, something that sounds a bit like radio chatter is heard, and seems to dive the voyage portion of the original song’s namesake home; all it is missing is the “beep” from old NASA transmissions. The song continues to slow down more and more until the 9:31 mark, where it culminates in an acoustic guitar solo which eventually transitions into an electric guitar solo. The electric guitar portion from 10:19 to 11:55 is my favorite part of the whole album. At the end, the tempo slows down to a crawl and the melody to千年幻想郷 ～ History of the Moon slowly starts to play. It slows down more and more and more until the final note is struck followed by silence. After a pause, the sound of breaking glass (presumably the spell featured in the game) is heard emptying into silence. I can’t properly explain this song in words. It needs to be experienced; my words do not do it justice. Everything works in this song, and it might be the single greatest Touhou arrangement I have ever heard.

月見草 is the final track on the album, but it is essentially just some very quiet tones to the melody of the same name in the game. It exists as a cool down to the epic of 竹取飛翔 ～ Lunatic Princess.

Listening to悠夜永翔 ～Endless Flight of Eternal Night feels like a journey. It has its highs and lows, triumph and defeat. The album is paced perfectly and is really meant to be played all at once in one sitting. The whole is far more than the sum of its parts. I don’t think I can possibly say anything else about this album, and I hope I have not set expectations too high. Give it a listen, and let me know if I’m just crazy with how good I think it is. I hope this mostly stream of consciousness review makes any sense at all. I mostly just listened to the album and put my thoughts down on the screen.

I played from youth through high school. Watched a couple of world cups but never really got into it again until my friend invited me to a Sounders game on Oct 31, 2010. I was hooked but shortly after moved to LA where I headed up the support group down there as a capo. Did that for 5 years before moving to Europe. Now I'm trying to start a support group here.

The game pulled me in bit by bit. I was in England for the 1994 World Cup. At first, I thought the zombie apocalypse must have occurred when the streets went silent (when I saw an empty London depicted in the movie 28 days later I thought…maybe there's just a game on), but I found out the people were all in pubs watching England play. I popped in for a few games and thought "well, this is fun." I then fell into coaching soccer during my brief stint as a teacher in the early 2000s and enjoyed getting into high school level tactics and can still picture the playing style of some of my better players. Fast forward to World Cup 2010 for THE MOMENT that sold me as a fan of the game for life. I was in my office streaming the morning U.S. vs. Algeria game, grumbling at having to work on contracts. I grabbed a buddy and asked if he would like to find a place to watch the second half on a big screen. The town was pretty quiet, since it was still morning, but I suggested that maybe the Irish bar was showing the game. When I opened the door, the USA fans were there in force with fans crammed in clearly in excess of the fire code. All were fairly sauced despite the early hour. My favorite guy was shirtless, schnockered, spilling whiskey, and draped in an American flag. I settled in with a Guinness and was treated to a miraculous penalty time goal by Landon Donavan streaking down the field and hammering the rebound into the net. The place erupted like no other viewing party I have ever seen before or since. Just rewatching that goa gives me shivers. After that, I started watching Premier League games, Champions League games, listening to the Total Soccer Show podcast (excellent resource for insightful discussion), and loving every minute. I am a season ticket holder for the Orlando City Soccer Club in our inaugural year and have had a ball watching every game with 3 buddies who have adjoining seats.
